jobDescription: Sablewood's identity platform handles sign-in for about two million users of its collaboration suite. The Technical Program Manager runs cross-team programmes on authentication features, keeps the plan and risk register, books security reviews, runs early-access programmes with customers and manages production launches: release approvals, launch-day coordination and post-launch incident handling. Status goes to engineering and product leadership every fortnight. The identity team has three engineering squads, and launches follow a written launch process with a go or no-go meeting.
requirements: Runs cross-team programmes with a maintained plan and risk register.
Coordinates security review for authentication features.
Has managed the production launch of a platform feature, including release approvals, launch-day coordination and post-launch incident handling.
Runs beta or early-access programmes with customers and synthesises feedback.
Reports programme status to engineering and product leadership.

evidence.text: Program Manager, Quayline Software: ran the passkey sign-in beta for 300 design-partner accounts in the preview environment; according to the head of product, passkeys went GA to every customer the following quarter.
Kept the passkey programme plan and risk register across the identity, mobile and support teams, reviewing open risks at a weekly 30-minute meeting, and kept the programme's decision log.

Booked and tracked the security architecture review and the external penetration test of the passkey flows, closing 11 findings with the identity engineers before the beta opened, and filed the test report in the security team's repository.

Gathered beta feedback through fortnightly calls with design partners and a tagged feedback board, and summarised the top issues for the identity team each sprint, ranked by the number of partners affected.
Sent a fortnightly status note to the VP of engineering and the identity product lead covering milestones, risks and decisions needed, keeping an archive of past notes.

Work sample: the beta programme plan for passkey sign-in, covering design-partner enrolment, preview-environment configuration, feedback channels and exit criteria for the beta; its section on general availability lists open questions only, such as support staffing and rollout order.
HR verification note: employment at Quayline Software as Program Manager from May 2022 to June 2024 was confirmed through the employer's verification service.

Reference check summary: Quayline's director of engineering confirmed in writing that the candidate ran the passkey beta and the security review track for it, and described the candidate's role as programme manager for the beta.

propositions.text: The candidate managed the production launch of passkey sign-in, which went GA to every customer, including release approvals and post-launch incident handling.
propositions.rationale: The general-availability statement is attributed to the head of product, and the documented work is a beta in the preview environment whose plan lists general availability as open questions. The deployment rule forbids describing a beta in a preview environment as a production launch, and the relayed remark does not say what the candidate managed.

propositions.text: The candidate ran the passkey sign-in beta with design partners, gathering feedback through fortnightly calls and a tagged feedback board.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the feedback work, the beta plan documents the preview-environment programme and the reference check confirms the candidate ran the beta.

propositions.text: The candidate coordinated the security architecture review and an external penetration test of the passkey flows, closing 11 findings before the beta opened.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the review track and the findings closed.

gold.expectedGap: Only the beta in the preview environment is documented; a production launch with release approvals, launch-day coordination and incident handling is not.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the beta, the security review track and the risk register work; record the general-availability remark as the head of product's words, not as a launch the candidate managed.
followUpTargets: Ask whether passkey sign-in reached general availability while the candidate was at Quayline, and which release approvals, launch-day tasks and post-launch incidents the candidate handled.
